clue.text: Big rat, hearing bow-legged waterfowl

indicators.note: hearing tells us the following words are to be judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: bow-legged is bandy and a coot is a waterbird, giving bandy coot

explanation.surface: Someone hears of a large rat and a waterbird with bandy legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' signals a homophone: BANDY COOT said out loud gives the Australian marsupial. The bandicoot is a rat-sized animal, and its name means 'pig-rat' in Telugu.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a large ratlike marsupial of Australia and South Asia.

clue.text: It's hell down there

parts.note: hell is traditionally the underworld lying beneath us, so the word for where it lies, down there, is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a complaint about a bad place, but simply says where hell is: underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is imagined as lying under the earth, the place down under.

clue.text: Drugs discovered in car cost phenomenal

indicators.note: phenomenal suggests something extraordinary happening, so these letters are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: Drugs found in a car cost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phenomenal' rearranges IN CAR COST; 'discovered' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs that dull the senses, often illegal ones.

clue.text: Shilly-shallying of French getting cut out

indicators.note: getting here means receiving inside, so the cut word takes in the French word

parts.note: an incision is a surgical cut, made to cut something out
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A Frenchman dithers about being cut out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' means the cut, INCISION, receives DE after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shilly-shallying is wavering, failing to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Linger longer, having old-fashioned Sunday on the river

parts.note: out of fashion is simply out
the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Someone lingers by an outdated Sunday riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; 'having' and 'on the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain beyond the expected time.

clue.text: The very least have need of money — that's by the way

parts.note: tin is slang for money
ie, id est, means that is
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The poorest need money, as a passing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have need of' and 'by' are links: tin, then ie for 'that's', then ST for the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiniest thing is the smallest of all, the very least in size.

clue.text: Giant gets periodical leave to return

parts.note: a periodical is a magazine, shortened to mag

indicators.note: to return asks for the word for leave to be read backwards

parts.note: to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A giant takes a magazine and is allowed to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns GO into OG. Gog and Magog are legendary giants, whose figures stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: In British legend this is one of a pair of giants guarding the City of London.

clue.text: Came galumphing into the club

indicators.note: galumphing is clumsy bounding, so these letters lumber into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stomped clumsily into the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galumphing' rearranges CAME; 'into' links. The club is a weapon, not a meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked staff used as a weapon.

clue.text: Newlywed given key to chamber

parts.note: G is a musical key
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A newly married man is handed the key to the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key but gives the musical key G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is a man just married or about to be.

clue.text: Talk gets almost commonplace over one's internal complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: gas is chatter, idle talk

indicators.note: almost says the word for commonplace loses its final letter

parts.note: trite means commonplace
one's is one is, read as I plus is

explanation.surface: Idle chatter grows trivial about someone's stomach trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of TRITE; 'one's' is I and IS shortened to IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, a bodily ailment.

clue.text: Gloomily threatening to take cover outside the old city

indicators.note: outside says the cover word goes round the city word

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, crosswords' favourite old city

explanation.surface: A dark menace is about to take a lid off an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take cover outside' puts LID around UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurid sky is ominous and glowing, sinister in its colour.

clue.text: Flung in to cause sticking

indicators.note: flung suggests the letters of the next words are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something hurled inward to make things adhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flung' rearranges the nine letters of IN TO CAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious things hold fast and keep a firm grip, like glue.

clue.text: Carver does improvisation of Duet to Crow

indicators.note: an improvisation makes the music up afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculptor improvises a duet for a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvisation of' rearranges the ten letters of DUET TO CROW; 'does' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes woodcuts carves blocks of timber for printing.

clue.text: Starting marriage with row about Khayyam

indicators.note: about says the rowing word goes round the letter from marriage

parts.note: you row with an oar

indicators.note: starting picks out the opening letter of the word marriage

explanation.surface: Someone begins married life with a quarrel concerning a Persian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' gives M and 'about' wraps OAR round it. 'row' reads as a quarrel but is the rowing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian poet of the Rubaiyat was named Omar Khayyam.

clue.text: Undressed old love in candlelight

parts.note: naked means undressed
an old flame is a former sweetheart

explanation.surface: A naked former lover is seen by candlelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle burns with an uncovered fire, the light of an exposed burning wick.

clue.text: King George I writing close to port

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
by means near, close to

explanation.surface: A king called George writes his letters near the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher for King George. Grimsby is a fishing port on the Humber estuary in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimsby is an English fishing harbour town on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Rain storm coming from the east, must put sticks round the flowers

indicators.note: round says the sticking word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to gum is to stick, so gums is sticks
E is short for east

indicators.note: storm suggests turbulence, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rainstorm blows in from the east, so the flowers must be staked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges RAIN to RANI, after E; GUMS goes 'round' them. 'sticks' looks like canes but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniums are popular garden and window-box flowering plants.

clue.text: Poles in characteristic conveyance

indicators.note: in says the poles go inside the characteristic word

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people are typically conveyed in a characteristic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' reads as people from Poland but gives N and S, the compass poles, which 'in' puts inside TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of people or goods from place to place.

clue.text: Honeybunch is not so much lacking in sweetness

parts.note: sugar and honeybunch are both terms of endearment
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is losing a little of her charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honeybunch' is a pet name; another is 'sugar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sugarless has no sugar added, so it is not sweet.

clue.text: Bit of rice is under your foot, from the meatball

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of the word rice

parts.note: the sole is the underside of your foot

explanation.surface: A grain of rice is stuck under your shoe, dropped from a meatball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' gives R, then IS and SOLE follow; 'from the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake or ball of minced meat.

clue.text: Honour for some, often no blessing

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being honoured is, for some people, often a mixed blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; the run spans the end of 'often', all of 'no' and the start of 'blessing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, conferring a title.

clue.text: Pawns piano and shelves

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
ledges are shelves

explanation.surface: Someone pawns their piano and their shelving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawns' looks like the noun but is the verb: to pawn is to pledge an item for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to give it as security, a promise of repayment.

clue.text: Sham before nurse

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A fake comes before a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To sham is to feign, to put on a false show.

clue.text: Parker is big in New York

definitions.note: Parker, in the stock phrase for a meddlesome busybody, stands for the adjective which that phrase opens with

indicators.note: in says the size letters go inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, meaning big

explanation.surface: Someone named Parker is a big name in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parker' reads as a surname but recalls Nosy Parker, a British phrase for a prying busybody. OS (outsize) goes 'in' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A prying busybody is called a Nosy Parker in British idiom, so the name suggests that adjective.

clue.text: Said to have been influenced by the leather

indicators.note: said to tells us the next words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: to have been influenced is to have been swayed

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to have been swayed by leather goods.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAYED, said out loud, sounds like the word for the soft leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a soft napped finish.

clue.text: One butting in when dozy inert ref shows hesitation

indicators.note: dozy means half-asleep and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A sleepy referee hesitates while a player butts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dozy' rearranges INERT REF into INTERFER, and ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who butts in meddles in others' affairs uninvited.

clue.text: Beam when non-drinker comes in irritable

indicators.note: comes in says the abstainer letters go inside the beam word

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
TT is teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: Someone smiles when the teetotaller arrives, being cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a smile but is a ray of light; TT, for teetotal, 'comes in' to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered, easily annoyed.

clue.text: Dupe gets the bird

definitions.meaning: to dupe is to trick or fool someone
a common seabird with white and grey plumage

explanation.surface: A fool is jeered off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being booed, but here it is a link plus the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to deceive them, and a seagull is a coastal seabird.

clue.text: Form queue, ban about fifty; getting disgruntled

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the numeral
form here is a verb meaning to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people are told to queue and then banned, and they grow grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' rearranges QUEUE BAN into UNEQUABE, which goes 'about' L. Unequable means not even-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: An unequable person is uneven of temper, hence grumpy and irritable.

clue.text: Man ignoring second danger warning

indicators.note: ignoring says a letter is left out of the man's name

parts.note: Albert is a man's name
B is the second letter, as in the second grade

explanation.surface: A man pays no heed to a second warning of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' gives ALBERT, and 'ignoring' drops B, for second-class or second grade.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal that warns of approaching danger.

clue.text: Suggest we shortly go back and put article in lift

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the turned suggestion word
go back means the suggestion word is read backwards

parts.note: let's is the short form of let us, a way to suggest we do something
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone proposes returning to put an item in the elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns LETS into STEL, and 'in' puts A inside. 'lift' looks like an elevator but means to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for pilfering it.

clue.text: Forever taking aim man gets cunning

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Les is a man's name
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A man spends ages taking aim and grows crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'gets' are links joining the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Endlessly means without stopping, for all time.
